title: Edges and triangles present the homotopy category of a quasicategory
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, standard simplices and degenerate simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $D$ be a quasicategory in a fixed universe. Define $hD$ to have the vertices of $D$ as objects and finite composable words of edges as morphisms, modulo the relations identifying a degenerate edge at $x$ with $1_x$ and identifying the word $(f,g)$ with $h$ whenever a $2$-simplex has edges $f$ on $[0,1]$, $g$ on $[1,2]$ and $h$ on $[0,2]$; composition is concatenation modulo these relations. Write $[f]$ for the morphism represented by an edge $f$. Every morphism $x\to y$ of $hD$ is $[f]$ for an edge $f:x\to y$ of $D$. For any vertices $x,y,z$ and edges $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to z$, $h:x\to z$, the equality $[g]\circ[f]=[h]$ in $hD$ holds if and only if there exists a $2$-simplex of $D$ with exactly these three edges. The assertion includes degenerate edges and empty quasicategories and holds in each input universe.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, July 30, 2026, Section 1.6, Lemma 1.6.2, Lemma 1.6.4 and Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp. 21-25 (PDF pp. 36-40). Theorem 1.6.6 identifies the edge-and-triangle presentation tau(D) with the category of homotopy classes of edges; Lemma 1.6.2 realizes composition equations by triangles. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.
